neighbours.label: Experimental-procedure text in science: the slot where a lab action is about to be stated (set up and ..., were used to characterize, try to reseat), as a predictor of procedure verbs (run, measure, perform), vs non-procedural sentences on other topics
fire: The technician sets up three flasks and adds a different buffer to each one.
XPS and SEM were used to analyze the surface of each coated wafer.
Students prepare two test tubes and heat them over the burner for five minutes.
Raman spectroscopy was used to identify the phases present in the films.
First calibrate the pH meter and then measure the acidity of each solution.
The cells were washed twice and then used to assess protein expression.
Load the samples into the centrifuge and spin them at high speed for ten minutes.
Infrared spectra were used to confirm the presence of the carbonyl group.
quiet: The children set up three tents and sang songs around the campfire.
Old photographs were kept in a box in the attic for many years.
Grandmother prepares two cakes and gives them to the neighbours each Sunday.
The painting was admired by visitors from many countries.
First buy the tickets and then meet your friends at the cinema.
The dogs were washed twice and then allowed to run in the garden.
Load the car with suitcases and drive to the beach for the weekend.
Holiday postcards were sent to all our relatives in December.

predictions: Connectives before a procedure verb in methods/instruction text reach 0.3-0.8; everyday sentences stay under 0.05. Descriptive sentences about lab samples may leak (probe 0.666).
notes: Card: peaks on ' and' in 'set up and simulate', ' to' in 'used to characterize', ' re' in reassign/reseat; - pole promotes run/measure/perform (the + pole suppresses them). Probe: 'set up five beakers and add' 0.712, 'used to characterize' 0.525, 'try to reseat' 0.439, 'set up and simulate' only 0.130; 'crystal structure of each sample was beautiful' 0.666 (leak: lab context alone fires); market control 0.015, tutorial history 0.012.
